tooltip.EWMA.title: Exponentially Weighted Moving Average
tooltip.EWMA.short: Ratio of acute (7-day) to chronic (28-day) training load.
tooltip.EWMA.long: Calculates the training load ratio, prioritizing recent workloads. A ratio between 0.8 and 1.3 is optimal. Higher values indicate elevated risk.
tooltip.RPE.title: RPE
tooltip.RPE.long: A subjective measure of intensity. RPE 10 is max effort (0 reps left). RPE 8 means you could have done 2 more reps.
tooltip.sRPE.title: sRPE
tooltip.sRPE.long: Calculated as Intensity x Duration. Tracks neurological and physical fatigue to optimize recovery protocols.
tooltip.CNS.title: CNS Load
tooltip.CNS.long: Heavy lifting drains your neural 'battery.' High CNS load requires lower intensity or longer rest to prevent burnout.
tooltip.1RM.title: 1RM %
tooltip.1RM.long: The baseline for your training blocks. Percentages (e.g., 70%) are calculated from your heaviest verified lift.
tooltip.Volume.title: Volume
tooltip.Volume.short: Total tonnage moved (Sets x Reps x Weight).
tooltip.Volume.long: A primary driver for hypertrophy. Tracking weekly accumulation helps manage progressive overload without overtraining.
tooltip.Readiness.title: Readiness
tooltip.Readiness.short: Your physical and psychological preparedeness for training.
tooltip.Readiness.long: Calculated based on recent volume, CNS load, and sleep data. A high Readiness score (80%+) suggests you are primed for high-intensity work.
tooltip.Sleep.title: Sleep Deficit
tooltip.Sleep.short: The physical and neurological cost of sub-optimal rest.
tooltip.Sleep.long: Cumulative sleep debt directly reduces neurological drive and force production. The deficit represents the calculated penalty based on recent sleep quality and volume recovery needs.
tooltip.Stress.title: Allostatic Load
tooltip.Stress.long: Life stress (work, psychological) competes for the same adaptive resources as training. High allostatic load reduces your recovery ceiling and increases injury risk.
tooltip.Percentile.title: Population Percentile
tooltip.Percentile.short: Your relative strength compared to the general population.
tooltip.Percentile.long: Calculated using ExRx.net's strength standards, which consider your gender, age, body weight, and total payload for the main lifts (Squat, Bench, Deadlift).
tooltip.jointStress.title: Joint Stress Balance
tooltip.jointStress.short: Ratio of high-impact work to low-impact recovery.
tooltip.jointStress.long: Tracks the structural cost of your training. Maintaining a balance between high-intensity loading and low-impact restoration is critical for long-term joint health and longevity.
tooltip.DeploymentObjectives.title: Deployment Objectives
tooltip.DeploymentObjectives.short: The primary goals of your training sequence.
tooltip.DeploymentObjectives.long: Pure Strength: Max force. Powerbuilding: Strength & size. Hypertrophy: Muscle growth. Longevity: Health & durability. Tactical: Field-ready fitness. Explosiveness: Power. Endurance: Stamina. Prehab: Injury prevention.
tooltip.ProgramImpact.title: Program Impact
tooltip.ProgramImpact.long: mTOR Interference: High-intensity aerobic work competes with hypertrophy pathways, potentially blunting maximum strength gains if programmed too closely together.
analysis.redlineMechanicalFailureRisk: Mechanical failure risk detected. System has enforced a 25% load reduction. Readiness scores have been suppressed in favor of structural integrity.
analysis.aerobicInterferenceWarning: Recent high-intensity recovery activity detected. System has applied a 15% CNS tax.
analysis.fatigueContextDesc: This mission contributes to your systemic fatigue score. Non-program activities with an RPE > 5 may impact your next heavy lifting mission by reducing your starting readiness score.
analysis.aiTipFatigue: You're accumulating too much systemic fatigue from extracurricular activities. Consider lowering the RPE of your tactical missions or reducing duration to preserve force production for the barbell.
analysis.aiTipOptimal: Keep tactical missions at an RPE of 7 or lower on days prior to lower-body training to prevent central nervous system fatigue.
analysis.mTorInterferenceTooltip: mTOR Interference: High-intensity aerobic work competes with hypertrophy pathways, potentially blunting maximum strength gains if programmed too closely together.

stage.terms.1.title: Physical Risk Acknowledgment
stage.terms.1.content: Physical fitness testing involves maximal efforts that place stress on the musculoskeletal and cardiovascular systems. You acknowledge that you are performing these movements at your own risk.
stage.terms.2.title: Equipment Integrity
stage.terms.2.content: You verify that all testing equipment and your environment are secure, in good working order, and appropriate for the test requirements.
stage.terms.3.title: Biometric Monitoring
stage.terms.3.content: These metrics are for informational purposes only and should not replace professional medical advice or your own internal perception of safety.
stage.terms.4.title: Safety Protocol
stage.terms.4.content: In the event of strain or failed movement, safely cease the activity immediately. Prioritize your physical safety over completing the exercise repetition.
stage.terms.5.title: Fatigue Management
stage.terms.5.content: High-intensity testing causes significant physical and neural demand. If the system detects performance degradation below the safety threshold, it may recommend aborting the assessment.
stage.terms.6.title: Data Privacy
stage.terms.6.content: Your performance data is encrypted and stored locally. Aggregated, anonymized data may be used to improve Vanguard's predictive algorithms.
stage.terms.7.title: Final Authorization
stage.terms.7.content: By clicking "Accept & Start", you authorize the initiation of the fitness assessment and confirm you are in a physical state capable of this exertion.
